title: The evidence base is graded, and the strong tier carries the argument
statement: 30 of 64 findings are graded strong; 27 support, 6 are caveats and 1 is weak.
detail: There are also 5 independent audit notes and 4 high-severity workspace issues. The ledger is the primary index; grades are researcher-assigned, not externally audited.
caveat: Grade definitions are operational and documented on the findings page.

title: Cross-boundary transfer is the binding model risk
statement: The final 27-feature model reaches PR-AUC 0.5575 on the held-out test split, while the same walk-forward design averages 0.9510 in-domain.
detail: Across four time-ordered folds, in-domain PR-AUC is 0.9510 ± 0.0152; the same models score 0.4726 ± 0.0761 across the boundary. Mean gap: 0.4785.
caveat: The test split is a temporal holdout, not a random sample from the same distribution.

title: Card history both drives ranking and explains the transfer failure
statement: Removing card_prior_fraud raises test PR-AUC from 0.5575 to 0.8315; the raw-only model reaches 0.8353.
detail: The ablation localises the largest change to cumulative card history. The direction is counter-intuitive but internally consistent: the full model's strongest in-domain signal is also the least portable across the time boundary.
caveat: Ablation variants are not independent experiments; they share training rows and the same test split.

title: A 1% review budget captures about two-thirds of fraud events and dollars
statement: Reviewing the top 1.0% of test transactions (5,557 reviews) captures 65.45% of fraud events and 68.70% of fraud dollars.
detail: Precision at that operating point is 25.27%; dollar yield is $140.11 per review. A 5% budget raises recall to 86.20% and dollar capture to 93.42% but requires 27,786 reviews.
caveat: Capture is measured on the held-out test split and depends on the stored score ranking.

title: Calendar encodings drift hardest across the time boundary
statement: 7 of 27 features have severe PSI (≥ 0.25); 1 is moderate and 19 are stable.
detail: The largest PSI is month_sin at 6.514, followed by n_prior at 5.095. Month and cyclical encodings dominate because the test window covers months unseen in training.
caveat: PSI thresholds are conventions, not statistical tests; high PSI identifies distribution shift, not a broken feature.

title: Amount separates fraud strongly, but the distributions still overlap
statement: Fraud amounts have a median of $390.00 versus $47.24 for genuine transactions (Cliff's delta 0.669).
detail: KS D is 0.724 with a bootstrap interval of 0.656–0.680 for Cliff's delta. The effect is large, but the overlap means amount alone cannot be a decision rule.
caveat: Cliff's delta is a rank effect size; it does not establish a causal amount effect.

title: The split is temporal, and the fraud rate drops at the boundary
statement: Train fraud rate is 0.579%; test is 0.386% — a drop of 0.193 percentage points.
detail: Train and test are separated by 48 seconds on 21 June 2020. Any random-split metric would answer a different question and should not be compared to these results.
caveat: The boundary is documented; the 48-second gap is not a causal treatment.

title: Structural missingness is concentrated in history features
statement: 11 columns are incomplete; the maximum is 10.79% for amt_z_prior and amt_z_prior_log.
detail: The missing values are first-transaction history fields. They are not random missingness and were not imputed in the dashboard; any feature using them inherits the boundary.
caveat: A zero in the dashboard means no recorded value, not a measured zero.

title: The learning curve is non-monotonic, so more training rows did not help
statement: Test PR-AUC peaks at 0.6266 with 324,168 training rows (fraction 0.25) and falls to 0.5254 on the full training set.
detail: The drop is consistent with a distribution shift: additional training-period rows do not make the test-period distribution more similar. It is not evidence that the model is unstable in the usual sense.
caveat: The learning curve is single-seed and uses one test split; it is not a learning-theory estimate.

title: The cost-minimising threshold is fragile to the false-positive charge
statement: Across false-positive costs from $1 to $50, the optimal threshold moves from 9.70e-07 to 4.31e-04 and recall falls from 91.6% to 70.2%.
detail: The threshold is not a stable operating constant. It should be re-derived for the review team's actual cost and capacity; the dashboard exposes the input.
caveat: Cost-minimisation assumes the stated FP charge and full fraud loss; neither is a production estimate.

title: Probability calibration is already accurate at this prevalence
statement: Temperature scaling fits T = 1.418; expected calibration error changes from 0.000159 to 0.000118.
detail: The absolute errors are tiny because the simulator is smooth and the test prevalence is low. Calibration is not the binding problem; ranking and transfer are.
caveat: ECE is computed on a calibration split; it does not guarantee calibration under a different prevalence.

title: The run completed without tracebacks but with seven skipped static exports
statement: The notebook reports 0 error events and 0 tracebacks; 7 static PNG exports were skipped.
detail: The skipped exports are an operational limitation, not an analytical failure. The interactive HTML artifacts survive and are linked from the gallery. No timestamps are available for these events.
caveat: Warnings are not failures; the run still reports zero tracebacks.

title: One leakage claim is contradicted by its own recorded numbers
statement: Audit note AN-01 reports that the naive and causal target-encoding correlations are both 0.048 at the displayed precision, so the notebook does not demonstrate the claimed inflation.
detail: The causal encoding remains good practice, but the specific leakage-demo claim should not be cited as evidence that the naive encoding inflated this dataset's signal.
caveat: Equality at three decimals does not prove the encodings are identical; it only shows the displayed evidence does not support inflation.

title: One finding remains in the weak tier and should not anchor a decision
statement: The ledger contains 1 weak finding: F-024 · Structural breaks in daily fraud-rate stable across PELT penalties (2 consensus breaks); holiday proximity: 0 coincidences — breaks are generator-campaign driven, not calendar-driven.
detail: The weak grade is not a contradiction; it marks a claim whose evidence is insufficient for confident reuse. The structural-break finding is the only member of this tier.
caveat: Grade assignment is researcher-assigned; the dashboard does not re-grade the evidence.

title: The final weekly bin is an edge case, not a fraud collapse
statement: The final recorded week (2021-01-03) shows 0 fraud events across 18,921 transactions, while the weekly median is around 0.507%.
detail: The last bin covers a partial boundary and is retained only because the notebook records it. It should be excluded from trend interpretation rather than read as a real decline.
caveat: The zero is a recorded count for the final bin; it is not evidence of zero fraud risk going forward.
